## Highlights

- **A session's browser takes your clicks, Enter and new tabs again.** In Session Manager, opening a running session and bringing the pointer down from the address bar into the page could leave its browser taking no mouse input at all: a click in the page did nothing, Enter in the address bar opened nothing, and the new-tab button stayed without effect. On Linux, the Camoufox browser could lose a mouse event on the first row of a page (with a Windows or macOS fingerprint) or on its last row (with a Linux fingerprint), and then took no mouse input again, in any of its tabs, until the session restarted. Session Manager now sends every mouse event at least one row inside the page, so the browser no longer gets such an event.
  - Should the browser still stop taking the mouse, Session Manager no longer waits for it without end. Once a mouse event has not been done five seconds after its page was free (no dialog waiting for an answer, no script keeping the page busy), the session's page says that the browser stopped responding to the mouse and that restarting the session brings the mouse back. Typing, addresses, back and forward and the tabs go on working meanwhile; a reload is refused for the same reason instead of waiting behind. An assistant working through Session Manager's MCP endpoint gets the same reason for a click, hover, scroll or drag.
- **The address bar stays where it is when you switch sessions.** While the next session's browser was being connected, its tab strip stood 6 pixels taller than it does with its tabs, so the address bar moved down and back up on every switch.

## Upgrade notes

- **Session Manager:** run the `tale-session-manager` image `0.5.103`. No configuration change. A session whose browser had already stopped taking the mouse takes it again once the session is restarted.
- **Platform:** no action. This release adds no migration, the API contract stays `3.53.0`, and no configuration or environment variable changes.
